_about: New York's big live venues for the Venues pages (engine/venues.py), with the three across the state and river lines that New Yorkers travel to (MetLife, Prudential Center, UBS Arena; "outside": no map, City parking or What's here for those). Hand-curated: capacity is the venue's usual figure and is only used to sort and to say 'about'; notes are plain arrival facts written from the venue's own pages. Events come from Ticketmaster's Discovery API (engine/fetch_venue_events.py nyc, venue by venue), matched by `tm` names near each venue's point; their ids are learned into raw/venue_tm_ids.json. Keep this a short list of the places most people travel to, not a directory.
week: Monday to Sunday, New York time

feed._about: engine/fetch_venue_events.py: venue by venue (a sweep of New York stops at 1,000 events, a few days' worth). drop: words left out when matching the feed's venue names to ours.

fares._about: Flat figures the pages quote. Check them before a release; they go stale. local is the MTA subway and bus fare (OMNY, from January 4, 2026). The taxi figures are the TLC yellow-cab meter: $3.00 to start and $0.70 a fifth of a mile ($3.50 a mile), plus the $0.50 MTA and $1.00 improvement surcharges every trip pays (taxiExtra). Sources: nyc.gov/tlc taxi-fare page; mta.info fares.
fares.oneFare: A taxi trip that starts, ends or passes through Manhattan below 96th Street adds $2.50, and $0.75 more below 60th Street; rush hour, overnight, tolls and tip are extra. OMNY caps subway and local bus fares at $35 for any 7 days.

page._about: How engine/venues.py reads New York: the map's subway and its commuter rail and PATH stations, City (NYC DOT) municipal parking, community districts as the units, and the hubs a trip from outside the city arrives at. lineHints: name the subway lines that run from a hub or origin to the venue's station.

parking.label: City parking
parking.note: NYC DOT’s municipal garages and fields; figures are capacities, not live availability. Venues’ own lots are described in the notes.

words.legend: Subway lines in their colours, commuter rail and PATH dashed, City parking in green squares, other venues in grey.
words.sources: Transit: MTA, NJ Transit and the Port Authority (PATH). Parking: NYC DOT.

venues.name: MetLife Stadium
venues.address: 1 MetLife Stadium Drive, East Rutherford, NJ
venues.season: Football runs from August to early January and stadium concerts are in summer; February to April is mostly quiet.
notes: On big event days NJ Transit runs Meadowlands Rail trains from Secaucus Junction to the stadium's own Meadowlands station, and riders show a valid train ticket at Secaucus to get a wristband.
Coach USA's 351 Meadowlands Express runs from the Port Authority Bus Terminal to Lot K.
The entrances are the AMEX, MetLife and Verizon gates; parking is paid, and only clear bags up to 12 x 6 x 12 inches (or a small clutch) are allowed, one per person.

transit.*: On event days, NJ Transit to Secaucus Junction (from Penn Station or Hoboken), then the Meadowlands train to the stadium; or Coach USA’s 351 from the Port Authority Bus Terminal

venues.arrive: Meadowlands Rail from Secaucus Junction on event days, or the 351 bus from Port Authority

venues.name: Yankee Stadium
venues.tickets: Yankees home games are sold by the team through MLB, not Ticketmaster, so they aren’t in this listing; concerts and NYCFC matches are.
venues.season: Open-air: baseball runs from April to September (October in a playoff year); it is quiet from November to March.
notes: The 4, B and D trains stop at 161 St-Yankee Stadium, and Metro-North's Yankees-E 153 St station is also steps from the gates; the B runs on weekdays only.

The gates are 2 (left field, Jerome Avenue and East 164th Street), 4 (home plate, East 161st Street), 6 (right field, East 161st Street and River Avenue) and 8 (centre field, River Avenue and East 164th Street).
One soft-sided bag up to 16 x 16 x 8 inches plus one small personal item is allowed, and the team does not run the paid garages nearby.

venues.name: Citi Field
venues.tickets: Mets home games are sold by the team through MLB, not Ticketmaster, so they aren’t in this listing; concerts are.
venues.season: Open-air: baseball runs from April to September (October in a playoff year); it is quiet from November to March.
notes: The 7 train and the LIRR Port Washington Branch both stop at Mets-Willets Point beside the ballpark.
The main entry is the Jackie Robinson Rotunda, with Left Field, Right Field and Bullpen gates as well (the Bullpen gate is on Seaver Way).
Backpacks are not allowed, other bags must be no larger than 16 x 16 x 8 inches and there is no bag check; paid game-day parking is in Lot F.

venues.name: Arthur Ashe Stadium
venues.address: USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, Flushing Meadows Corona Park
tm: USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center
venues.season: The US Open fills it in late August and early September; the rest of the year it seldom has ticketed events.
notes: The 7 train and LIRR Port Washington Branch trains stop at Mets-Willets Point, and from there a boardwalk leads to the Main Entry.
Rideshare drop-off is in the New York Hall of Science lot, with a path to the Champion's Entry.
Both entrances screen bags, and large bags are not allowed.

venues.name: Madison Square Garden
notes: Above Penn Station, between Seventh and Eighth Avenues from 31st to 33rd Street, so the LIRR, NJ Transit and the 1, 2, 3, A, C and E trains stop underneath.
The Chase entrances are on Eighth Avenue, and there is a Seventh Avenue entrance too.
The Garden has no parking of its own; drivers use nearby commercial garages.

venues.name: UBS Arena
notes: LIRR trains from Grand Central Madison and Penn Station reach Elmont-UBS Arena station in about 30 minutes, then it is a 10 to 15 minute walk or a free shuttle to the arena.
Parking is paid, in lots reached only from the Cross Island Parkway (exits 26A, 26B and 26D), and drivers must leave the way they came.
Bags up to 12 x 12 x 6 inches are allowed; backpacks of any size are not, and there is a bag check in the Acrisure Great Hall.

transit.*: LIRR to Elmont-UBS Arena (about 30 min from Penn Station or Grand Central Madison; from elsewhere on Long Island, change at Jamaica), then a 10 to 15 min walk or the free shuttle

venues.arrive: LIRR to Elmont-UBS Arena, then a 10 to 15 min walk or the free shuttle

venues.name: Prudential Center
notes: Two blocks west of Newark Penn Station, which NJ Transit rail, PATH and the Newark Light Rail serve.
The entrances are Citizens Tower (Mulberry Street and Edison Place), M&M's Tower (Mulberry and Lafayette) and the Lafayette Street entrance.
Bags larger than 14 x 12 x 6 inches and backpacks are not allowed, and there are paid lockers outside; prepaid parking is sold for lots within walking distance.

transit.*: NJ Transit from Penn Station, or PATH from 33rd Street or the World Trade Center, to Newark Penn Station, then about 10 min on foot
transit.Newark: From Newark Penn Station, about 10 min on foot
transit.Princeton: NJ Transit from Princeton Junction to Newark Penn Station, then about 10 min on foot
transit.Hoboken: PATH from Hoboken to Newark Penn Station, changing at Journal Square, then about 10 min on foot
transit.Jersey City (Journal Square): PATH from Journal Square to Newark Penn Station, then about 10 min on foot

venues.name: Barclays Center
notes: Above the Atlantic Av-Barclays Ctr subway station (2, 3, 4, 5, B, D, N, Q, R) and across from the LIRR's Atlantic Terminal.
The main Atrium entrance is at the corner of Flatbush and Atlantic Avenues, and there are also Flatbush, Atlantic and Dean Street entrances.
Backpacks and bags larger than 10 x 6 x 2 inches are not allowed, and the venue says parking nearby is very limited.

transit.Hicksville: LIRR from Hicksville to Atlantic Terminal, changing at Jamaica; the arena is across the street
transit.Babylon: LIRR from Babylon to Atlantic Terminal, changing at Jamaica; the arena is across the street
transit.Ronkonkoma: LIRR from Ronkonkoma to Atlantic Terminal, changing at Jamaica; the arena is across the street

venues.name: Forest Hills Stadium
venues.season: Open-air: concerts run from late spring to early autumn; it is quiet in winter.
notes: The entrance is on Burns Street near 69th Avenue, a few blocks from the Forest Hills-71 Av subway station and next to the LIRR's Forest Hills station.
There is no parking at the venue or on the residential streets around it, and taxis and rideshares use 71st/Continental Avenue at Queens Boulevard.
Bags up to 16 x 16 x 8 inches are allowed, and larger bags must be checked for a fee.

venues.name: Radio City Music Hall
notes: On Sixth Avenue between 50th and 51st Streets in Rockefeller Center, with the box office under the marquee at 50th Street.
Bags must fit under the seat, bags larger than 22 x 14 x 9 inches are not allowed, and there is no bag or coat check.
There is no venue parking; drivers use nearby commercial garages.

venues.name: Metropolitan Opera House
venues.tickets: Sells through the Met’s own box office and website rather than Ticketmaster, so its performances aren’t in this listing.
notes: At Lincoln Center, between West 62nd and 65th Streets and Columbus and Amsterdam Avenues; the Met points people to the 1 train at 66 St-Lincoln Center.
A public garage under Lincoln Center has entrances on West 62nd and West 65th Streets and on Amsterdam Avenue.

venues.name: Kings Theatre
notes: On Flatbush Avenue between Tilden and Duryea, a short walk from Beverley Rd (Q) and Church Av (B, Q).
Bags must be 18 x 14 x 9 inches or smaller.
Street parking is limited, and the public lot behind the theatre is not run by the venue.

venues.name: Beacon Theatre
notes: On Broadway between West 74th and 75th Streets.
Bags must fit under the seat, and bags larger than 22 x 14 x 9 inches are not allowed.
There is no venue parking; drivers use nearby commercial garages.

venues.name: Carnegie Hall
venues.tickets: Sells through its own box office and website rather than Ticketmaster, so its concerts aren’t in this listing.
notes: At 57th Street and Seventh Avenue, where the box office is.
The stations the hall lists are 57 St-7 Av, 57 St on Sixth Avenue, 7 Av and 59 St-Columbus Circle.
Parking is in commercial garages on West 56th and West 57th Streets.

venues.name: Hammerstein Ballroom
notes: On West 34th Street between Eighth and Ninth Avenues, a block west of Penn Station.
The box office opens only for some events, and only after doors.

venues.name: Terminal 5
notes: Near Eleventh Avenue; the nearest subway stations are 59 St-Columbus Circle (A, B, C, D, 1) and 50 St (C, E).
Small bags are allowed and searched, and bags larger than 14 x 14 inches are not.
There is no parking on site.

venues.name: Brooklyn Paramount
notes: At Flatbush Avenue Extension and DeKalb Avenue, across the street from DeKalb Av (B, Q, R), with Nevins St (2, 3, 4, 5) about 0.2 miles away.
Allowed bags are clear ones up to 12 x 6 x 12 inches or a small bag up to 6 x 9 inches, and larger bags must be checked for a fee.
Tickets are mobile only, and parking is in nearby garages.
